case.title: Gresmoor police must delete old abortion records
case.question: How should Gresmoor Police find and delete its old abortion records without women having to ask?
case.story: From 16 November the law pardons women who were convicted, cautioned, arrested or investigated over their own abortion. Women do not have to apply. Gresmoor Police (made up) thinks it holds 9 such records, spread over paper files in a store, an old computer system and copies sent to the court. Some women have moved away, some have married and changed names, and some do not know a file exists. The force has £90,000 set aside and a records team of four. Nobody wants a clumsy search to leak a name or to wake a woman with a letter her family might open.

in_the_news.headline: Women pardoned for abortion offences relating to their own pregnancy
in_the_news.why: The new law makes police and courts delete these records, and a force like Gresmoor has to do it without women applying.

facts.text: Section 242 of the Crime and Policing Act 2026 pardons these women automatically from 16 November 2026. Women do not need to apply.
Where records cannot be fully deleted, they must be annotated so they are treated as deleted.

sources.title: Women pardoned for abortion offences relating to their own pregnancy
Section 242 of the Crime and Policing Act 2026: abortion offence pardons

made_by.note: Round 2, after review: the real guidance aims to delete records within one month, so t1's date moved from 28 February 2027 to 16 December 2026, and answer A's finish date with it. Every answer was then marked again from scratch by a fresh checker.

tests.text: Gives a finish date no later than 16 December 2026 for deleting or marking every record.
Names one job-holder who signs off each deletion and whom a woman can call with questions.
Never writes to, phones or visits a woman unless she has first asked to be contacted.
Says who pays and keeps the total within the £90,000 already set aside.
No woman's name or file detail goes to any outside firm or person.
Searches the paper store, the old system and the court copies, and has someone outside the records team check a sample.

voices.text: If it was me, I would want it gone and I would not want a letter turning up at my mum's door.
Women of my age remember when this could ruin you. Delete it properly and tell nobody who doesn't need to know.

voices.who: a woman, 26, looking after her family
voices.text: Say a date, say a name, and let us ring that person. That's all I'd ask.
Don't hire some firm to rummage through it. Keep it inside the police and check it twice.
I don't want my council tax spent on a fancy system. There's money set aside, so use it and finish the job.

bench.angle: Full sweep by the records team, with an outside check
bench.title: Inside sweep of all three stores, with an outside check
bench.answer: Gresmoor Police will search the paper store, the old system and the court copies, then delete each record or mark it as deleted. Finish date: 16 December 2026. The Head of Records signs off every deletion and answers calls from any woman with questions. The four-person records team does all the work, with no outside firm. No name or file detail leaves the police. An officer from outside the records team checks a sample of each store. We never write to, phone or visit a woman unless she asks first. Pay comes from the £90,000 already set aside, with a spending cap of £90,000. Success means every record is deleted or marked by the finish date, the checker finds no misses, and the force publishes only a record count.

bench.angle: Hire a sealed-room contractor to do the search
bench.title: Use a sealed-room contractor to search fast, under strict limits
bench.answer: Gresmoor Police hires one vetted contractor to run the search in a sealed room inside police premises. Staff are police-vetted and sworn to secrecy. No file, name or detail leaves the building. The contractor searches the paper store, the old system and the court copies, then deletes or marks each record. Finish by 31 January 2027. The Head of Records signs off every deletion and takes calls on a published number. The force pays from the £90,000 set aside, capped at £75,000. Nobody writes to, calls or visits any woman unless she asks first. A police inspector outside the records team checks a sample. Success means every record is deleted or marked, and the sample shows no misses.

bench.angle: Wait for requests and delete case by case
bench.title: Delete abortion records only when a woman asks
bench.answer: Gresmoor Police will not search for records. A woman who wants hers gone can ask by phone, post or online form. The records team then finds the file in the paper store, old system and court copies. It deletes it or marks it as deleted, and finishes each request within 28 days. The head of records, named on the force website, signs off every deletion and takes calls. Cost comes from the £90,000 already set aside, mostly for a small request line. No outside firm sees any names. A second officer checks a sample of cases. We would know it worked by counting requests met on time. Nobody gets an unwanted letter. Women who never hear of the offer keep their records, which is a gap.

gate.verdict: Only A meets every test and limit, including the 16 December date and the outside sample check. B misses the date and lets an outside contractor handle names, and C never sweeps the stores and leaves unrequested records in place.

jury.question: When the deleting is done, how much should Gresmoor Police tell the town?
options: Publish only the number of records deleted
Tell only the police oversight board
Say nothing unless a woman asks
jury.ruling: The town hears the number and nothing else, 7 to 4 to 1.

reasons.text: Show us it was done. A number, no names.
I'd rather it stayed inside the force.
Publish the count. People can trust what they can see.

minister.text: Gresmoor Police adopts Answer A: search all three stores, delete or mark every record by 16 December 2026, no outside firm, no letters unless a woman asks, all inside the £90,000.
minister.statement: This answer passed all six of the citizens' tests, both red lines included: no contact unless a woman asks, and no names to any outside firm. The jury ruled 7 to 4 to 1 that the town hears only the number deleted. I sign it. Done safely is what makes people safe, so the Head of Records answers the phone and the count goes public when the work is done.

predictions.claim: On 31 January 2027 the Ministry of Justice guidance on the abortion pardon will still say that police and courts aim to delete or mark records within 1 month, and will not try to contact women.
predictions.rule: Ministry of Justice guidance 'Section 242 of the Crime and Policing Act 2026: abortion offence pardons' on GOV.UK, read on 31 January 2027. True if it still says police and courts aim to delete or mark records within 1 month and will not try to contact women. Withdrawn: void.
